summary: preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes shipped obfuscated bundle
details: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin-processors-stub@12.8.19 advertises itself as a trivial ESLint processors stub but ships a preinstall hook (`scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`) that downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/`, extracts the platform-specific binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, string-array rotation function, numeric-index lookup table, mangled identifiers) whose behavior is not statically verifiable and is unrelated to the ESLint stub the package advertises. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute a large opaque bundle at install time — in a package whose stated purpose does not require Bun — matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern used to evade Node-based scanners; installing the package causes attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's machine under Bun.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
